Reproducibility: For the blocking review finding, the source path is clear: loadBlankPage awaits only delegate callbacks or cancellation with no timeout. I did not run a live WebKit failure harness, so this is source-reproducible rather than runtime-reproduced.

target.title: build: update Turndown to 7.2.4
target.body:
## Summary

- update the bundled Turndown distribution from 7.2.2 to 7.2.4
- initialize the WebKit runtime through a real navigation completion and serialize first use
- cover upstream link/image escaping fixes and concurrent initialization

## Upstream provenance

- repository: https://github.com/mixmark-io/turndown
- release comparison: https://github.com/mixmark-io/turndown/compare/v7.2.2...v7.2.4
- package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/turndown/v/7.2.4
- bundled payload SHA-256 after removing Demark's five-line license banner: `c97187f436d41638bf7acf346a39d9d42f2f2c02af18245a297c09e796f8e46f` (matches the official npm tarball)

## Risk

Medium. The generated vendor file is a large mechanical diff; the Swift runtime changes fix two integration hazards exposed by the new bundle: constructor export after evaluation and concurrent first-use navigation. Public API unchanged.

Files: 4. Diff: +272/-390.

## Proof

- `swift build -v`
- `swift test -v` — 59 tests passed; live suites skipped by default
- `DEMARK_LIVE_TESTS=1 swift test --filter DemarkURLLoading` — 26 tests passed
- `./scripts/lint.sh`
- `(cd Example && swift build -v)`
- source-blind external consumer: escaping, simple conversion, and concurrent first-use contracts passed
- exact reviewed tree equals the canonical branch tree
- autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
- public model identifier gate: PASS
